function.mechanism: Acts as a solvent/carrier for flavours and additives and, at sufficient concentration, exerts antimicrobial effects.
common_food_categories: pizza crust antimicrobial treatment (US-specific use condition)
foods with endogenous fermentation ethanol (e.g., some baked goods, fruit products)

adi.basis: No EFSA E1510-specific scientific opinion/ADI could be retrieved in this VM session due EFSA search endpoint access limitations (403/429).

efsa.key_finding: No retrievable EFSA re-evaluation specific to E1510 was identified during this run; EFSA search pages returned access/inaccessibility responses.

fda.notes: Section affirms specific GRAS use of ethyl alcohol as an antimicrobial agent on pizza crusts before final baking, not exceeding 2.0% by product weight.

adi.basis: ADI listed as LIMITED BY GMP (use as solvent, 1970); page also notes no safety concern at current intake for flavouring-agent context at the 46th meeting (1996).

concerns.summary: IARC classifies ethanol in alcoholic beverages as Group 1 carcinogenic to humans; epidemiological evidence links alcohol use with increased cancer risk (including EOCRC meta-analysis signal).
Low-dose food exposure studies found that while most foods were not high-risk acutely, some chronic exposure scenarios and child-focused puree scenarios may exceed study-derived thresholds.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA entry states LIMITED BY GMP for solvent use and includes a 1996 committee note of no safety concern at current intake for flavouring-agent context.
A 2023 low-dose food ethanol risk assessment reported low acute concern for most sampled foods.

populations: infants and young children with high intake of certain fruit purees
high chronic consumers of foods with endogenous/added ethanol
adi_exceedance.notes: No numeric EFSA ADI was retrievable; JECFA uses GMP-limited approach. Study-level analyses indicate potential exceedance of derived low-dose guidance values in some scenarios.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory frameworks permit use with constraints (FDA specific use condition; JECFA GMP-limited basis), but carcinogenic hazard context for ethanol and some low-dose/chronic exposure findings (especially in children under specific consumption assumptions) support a cautious middle-tier classification rather than risk_free/limited.
key_factors: FDA 21 CFR 184.1293 specific GRAS use condition
JECFA ADI basis: LIMITED BY GMP
IARC Group 1 listing for ethanol in alcoholic beverages
PubMed low-dose food exposure studies showing scenario-dependent concerns
